auth.description: Atlassian API token; the user half is the account email that minted it. This is the same token a Jira connection uses, but it is stored at a separate address and must be supplied again
auth.name: confluence.api_token
auth.subject: unstated

auth.description: Scoped Atlassian service-account API token. Carries the service account's own identity rather than a person's, and travels as a bearer credential with no user half
auth.name: confluence.service_api_token
auth.subject: app

config.help: Your Atlassian site's cloud id — the UUID your own site reports at `https://<your-site>.atlassian.net/_edge/tenant_info`. It is the same value your Jira connection uses, if you have one; Confluence and Jira are two products of one cloud tenant
config.label: Atlassian cloud id
config.name: cloud_id

config.help: The email of the account that minted the API token. It travels as the username half of the request
config.label: Atlassian account email
config.name: email

config.help: Create one at id.atlassian.com under Security → API tokens. Atlassian shows it once. This is the same kind of token a Jira connection uses — and if you already made one for Jira, that token works here too, but it has to be pasted again: the two connections store it separately
config.label: API token
config.name: api_token

description: Confluence Cloud wiki: find spaces, list the pages in one, read a page's metadata, publish a new page, and comment on one. Page and comment *content* cannot be read back — see the connector's notes

contract.description: List the site's global spaces, with the id, key and name of each. This connector's `verify`: a bounded read that runs unattended and needs nothing configured beyond the cloud id and the credential. `limit` caps the page at Confluence's maximum of 100; `start` walks past it. Personal spaces are excluded by a pinned `type` — a site's personal spaces are one per member and are not what a caller listing spaces is looking for

operations.description: List the site's global spaces, with the id, key and name of each. This connector's `verify`: a bounded read that runs unattended and needs nothing configured beyond the cloud id and the credential. `limit` caps the page at Confluence's maximum of 100; `start` walks past it. Personal spaces are excluded by a pinned `type` — a site's personal spaces are one per member and are not what a caller listing spaces is looking for

params.description: Which kind of space to list. Pass `global` for a site's team spaces; omitting it also returns the one-per-member personal spaces, which on a large site fill the first page. **Not pinned, although it should be**: this connector declares it `const = "global"`, and the document generator drops a `const` from both the request template and the input schema rather than emitting the literal, so the value has to be sent by the caller
params.name: type

params.description: Maximum spaces to return in one page. Confluence defaults to 25 and caps at 100
params.name: limit

params.description: How many spaces to skip, for walking past the first page. Confluence pages this surface by offset rather than by cursor, so unlike the v2 surface it can actually be followed
params.name: start

_links.description: `base` is the site URL and `next` is the relative URL of the following page, present only when there is one. Unlike the v2 surface's opaque cursor, the offset it carries is reproducible with `start`

_expandable.description: What Confluence would return if asked to expand it. This connector asks for none of it, so every value here is a path rather than data

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the space's path in the Confluence UI — append it to the site URL to give a human a link

id.description: The space's numeric id. Note the v1 surface types this as a number where the v2 surface typed it as a string

key.description: The space key, e.g. `ENG` — the short code in a Confluence URL, and what `confluence-space-get` and `confluence-space-pages` address a space by on this surface

type.description: `global` here, because this operation pins it

size.description: How many spaces are in **this page** — not the site total, which this surface does not report

start.description: The offset this page began at

contract.description: Get one space by its key, with its name, type and status. Addressed by the space **key** — the short code that appears in a Confluence URL — because that is what this surface routes on; the numeric id is returned rather than accepted

operations.description: Get one space by its key, with its name, type and status. Addressed by the space **key** — the short code that appears in a Confluence URL — because that is what this surface routes on; the numeric id is returned rather than accepted

params.description: The space key, e.g. `ENG`, from `confluence-space-list`'s `key`. Not the numeric id
params.name: space_key

_expandable.description: Paths Confluence would expand if asked; this connector asks for none

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the space's path in the Confluence UI, and `base`, the site URL to resolve it against

key.description: The space key that was passed in

status.description: `current` or `archived`. An archived space still reads

type.description: `global` for an ordinary space or `personal` for a member's own

contract.description: List the pages in one space, with the id, title and status of each — the way to discover what a space contains and to resolve a page title to the id `confluence-page-get` takes. **Page bodies are not returned here**; ask for one page at a time. `limit` caps the page at Confluence's maximum of 100 and `start` walks past it

operations.description: List the pages in one space, with the id, title and status of each — the way to discover what a space contains and to resolve a page title to the id `confluence-page-get` takes. **Page bodies are not returned here**; ask for one page at a time. `limit` caps the page at Confluence's maximum of 100 and `start` walks past it

params.description: The space key, e.g. `ENG`, from `confluence-space-list`'s `key` — not the numeric id
params.name: space_key

params.description: Which kind of content to list. Pass `page`; omitting it also returns blogposts, comments and attachments. Declared `const`, and unpinned for the reason `confluence-space-list`'s `type` states
params.name: type

params.description: Maximum pages to return in one page of results. Confluence defaults to 25 and caps at 100
params.name: limit

params.description: How many results to skip, for walking past the first page
params.name: start

_links.description: `base` is the site URL; `next` is the relative URL of the following page when there is one

results.description: This page's content items, all of type `page` because the operation pins it

_expandable.description: Paths Confluence would expand if asked — `body`, `version`, `space`, `ancestors`. This connector asks for none of them here, so a page's body and its place in the tree come from `confluence-page-get`

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the page's path in the Confluence UI — the link to give a human, resolved against the site URL

id.description: The page's id, as a string — what `confluence-page-get` and `confluence-comment-add` address it by

title.description: The page's title. The only content-bearing field this operation returns, and what a title-to-id lookup matches on

size.description: How many items are in **this page** of results

contract.description: Read one page by id — its title, status, current version, the link to open it in Confluence, **and its body**. The body comes back as Confluence storage format, XHTML-like markup rather than Markdown, because this operation pins the `expand` that asks for it. That is the difference between this and the surface this connector shipped before 2026-09-04, which could return only metadata and an empty `body`

operations.description: Read one page by id — its title, status, current version, the link to open it in Confluence, **and its body**. The body comes back as Confluence storage format, XHTML-like markup rather than Markdown, because this operation pins the `expand` that asks for it. That is the difference between this and the surface this connector shipped before 2026-09-04, which could return only metadata and an empty `body`

params.description: The page's id, from `confluence-space-pages`, from a link, or from `confluence-page-create`'s response
params.name: id

params.description: What Confluence should include beyond the page's metadata. Pass `body.storage,version` to get the page's content and its current version; omitting it returns a page with no readable body at all, which is what this connector could only ever do before. Declared `const`, and unpinned for the reason `confluence-space-list`'s `type` states
params.name: expand

_expandable.description: Paths Confluence would expand if asked, beyond the two this operation pins

_links.description: `webui` is the page's path in the Confluence UI and `base` is the site URL — join them to give a human a link. `tinyui` is Confluence's short form

body.description: The page's content, present because this operation pins `expand=body.storage`

storage.description: The page in **Confluence storage format**: XHTML-like markup, not Markdown and not rendered HTML

id.description: The page's id, as a string

type.description: `page` for a page, `blogpost` for a blog post — this operation addresses content by id and does not constrain the kind

version.description: The page's current version, present because this operation pins `expand=version`

by.description: Who made the most recent edit. Identifies a named person: read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

message.description: The edit comment, when the editor left one

minorEdit.description: Whether the editor marked it a minor edit, suppressing notifications

number.description: The current version number — what an update would have to increment. This connector declares no update

when.description: When this version was created, i.e. when the page was last edited

contract.description:
Publish a new page in a space. The page is created live and visible to everyone who can see the space, is indexed for search, and notifies the space's watchers. It is created at the top level of the space unless the space's own structure places it otherwise, with no labels and no restrictions. Returns the new page's id, title and links. The content is sent as Confluence storage format — XHTML-like markup, e.g. `

text

` — not Markdown and not wiki markup

operations.description:
Publish a new page in a space. The page is created live and visible to everyone who can see the space, is indexed for search, and notifies the space's watchers. It is created at the top level of the space unless the space's own structure places it otherwise, with no labels and no restrictions. Returns the new page's id, title and links. The content is sent as Confluence storage format — XHTML-like markup, e.g. `

text

` — not Markdown and not wiki markup

params.description: Id of the space to publish into, from `confluence-space-list`. The only field Confluence's schema strictly requires
params.name: space_id

params.description: The page's title, as it will appear in the space and in search. Confluence requires titles to be unique within a space and rejects a duplicate with a `400`
params.name: title

params.description:
The page content, in **Confluence storage format**: XHTML-like markup such as `

A paragraph.

A heading

  • An item
`. Plain text is accepted and renders as a single unformatted run. Markdown is **not** converted — it would be stored and displayed literally, asterisks and all
params.name: body

_links.description: `webui` is the new page's path in the Confluence UI and `base` is the site URL; join them to give a human the link to what was just published

authorId.description: The account the token belongs to — a published page is attributed to it, and that name is what other people in the space will see

body.description: Echoes the storage-format content that was sent, under `storage`. This is the one response in this connector that carries a page body — because it is the body the caller supplied, not one Confluence was asked to render

id.description: The new page's id — the only handle on it, and what `confluence-comment-add` and `confluence-page-get` address it by afterwards

parentId.description: The page it was placed under, which Confluence resolves to the space's home page when none was requested

spaceId.description: The space the page was published into

status.description: `current` on a page this operation created

title.description: Echoes the title that was sent

version.description: `{number, createdAt, authorId, minorEdit, message}`, with `number` = 1 on a page just created

contract.description:
Add a footer comment to a page — the comment thread at the bottom, not an inline annotation on selected text. The comment is visible to everyone who can see the page and notifies its watchers; it cannot be restricted to a subset of them. The content is sent as Confluence storage format (`

text

`), not Markdown. Note the page is named in the body rather than in the path, and that this connector cannot read a page's existing comments back

operations.description:
Add a footer comment to a page — the comment thread at the bottom, not an inline annotation on selected text. The comment is visible to everyone who can see the page and notifies its watchers; it cannot be restricted to a subset of them. The content is sent as Confluence storage format (`

text

`), not Markdown. Note the page is named in the body rather than in the path, and that this connector cannot read a page's existing comments back

params.description: Id of the page to comment on, from `confluence-space-pages` or `confluence-page-create`. This creates a top-level footer comment on that page; replying to an existing comment is not supported by this operation
params.name: page_id

params.description:
The comment text, in **Confluence storage format**: XHTML-like markup such as `

A comment.

`. Plain text is accepted and renders unformatted. Markdown is **not** converted and would be displayed literally
params.name: body

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the comment's anchored path in the Confluence UI — it opens the page scrolled to this comment — and `base`, the site URL to resolve it against

body.description: Echoes the storage-format content that was sent, under `storage`

id.description: The new comment's id, as a string

pageId.description: The page the comment was attached to — echoes what was sent, and worth checking, since the parent is chosen by which body field was present rather than by the path

parentCommentId.description: Null on a top-level comment, which is all this operation creates

title.description: Confluence's own generated title for the comment, e.g. `Re: <page title>`. Not something the caller sets

version.description: `{number, createdAt, authorId, minorEdit, message}`, with `number` = 1 on a comment just created
